context:
Overall review topic: the impact of large language models (ChatGPT-style chatbots, AI answer engines, AI shopping assistants) on CONSUMER SEARCH, and how to better design or use LLMs for consumer search; spanning economics, marketing and CS. This is a FOLLOW-UP round. Seven initial streams already ran. BEFORE searching, read the existing workbench files named below so you do not re-report papers already found; report only NEW papers (you may cite existing ones briefly as context).

Round-0 findings so far (one line each): (01) Econ: 2026 theory models AI agents as cheaper Weitzman searchers; no LLM-specific study with real market data on price dispersion or concentration found. (02) Consumer evidence: 11 small lab/online studies; LLM search cuts time and queries, accuracy drops when LLM errs; field evidence on purchases and substitution conflicts. (03) LLM answer engines cut publisher clicks 35-48%; LLM ad auctions only theory/simulation; GEO up to +40% visibility in benchmarks. (04) LLM recs concentrate on incumbent brands; vary by persona and run; strategic text raises rec rate; no SSRN/NBER papers found. (05) LLM shopping agents show position bias and anchoring; decoy results conflict; benchmarks show low success. (06) Deployed design gains are small: LLM query rewriting +0.40% GMV Taobao, LLM-judge distillation +0.8% add-to-cart Walmart, generative retrieval ~1-2% GMV; search hit its round cap. (07) Citations raise trust even when wrong; hedging and confidence highlighting help; shallower learning.

Existing workbench files: /home/ubuntu/ml-best-practices/docs/lit_review/2026-11-03-llm-consumer-search/workbench/agents/*.md

Today is 2026-11-03. Include 2025-2026 working papers (SSRN, NBER, arXiv econ.GN, CEPR) and conference papers (EC, WWW, KDD, SIGIR, CHI, Marketing Science conference).

streams.title: Real-world evidence: does LLM search replace web search and change purchases?
streams.question: What field and observational evidence (clickstream panels such as Comscore or Similarweb, browser logs, platform data, natural experiments such as Italy's 2023 ChatGPT ban, staggered rollouts of AI Overviews or Amazon Rufus, retailer referral data) shows whether LLM tools substitute for or complement traditional web search, and how they change real consumer purchase outcomes, conversion, basket composition, or spending?
streams.extra: Read first: workbench/agents/02_consumer_use_evidence.md and 03_search_engines_publishers_geo.md. Output file names use prefix f1_1.

streams.title: Economics and marketing working papers on generative AI and consumer markets
streams.question: Sweep SSRN, NBER, CEPR and top marketing/IS/econ journals (Marketing Science, JMR, JM, Management Science, ISR, MISQ, QJE, AER, RAND) for 2023-2026 papers on generative AI or LLMs and consumer search or product choice: market concentration and long-tail effects, price competition, brand strategy and advertising in AI answers, consumer welfare, platform self-preferencing, and empirical studies using LLMs to measure consumer search. Which papers exist that the CS-leaning searches missed?
streams.extra: Read first: workbench/agents/01_econ_search_theory.md and 04_brand_bias_manipulation.md. Use WebSearch with site:ssrn.com, site:nber.org and journal names. Output file names use prefix f1_2.

streams.title: Deployed LLM shopping assistants and generative retrieval: what works at scale
streams.question: Complete the coverage of deployed LLM systems for product search: generative retrieval and semantic-ID methods, LLM query rewriting, and conversational shopping assistants deployed in production (Amazon Rufus, Instacart, Shopify, Walmart, Alibaba, JD, Meituan, Etsy, eBay, Zalando). What architectures, online A/B results and lessons (latency, hallucination, cost) are reported?
streams.extra: Read first: workbench/agents/06_system_design_ir.md (32 papers already found; it hit its round cap while still finding generative-retrieval and query-rewriting papers). Output file names use prefix f1_3.

streams.title: Designing LLM shopping help that serves the consumer
streams.question: What research proposes and tests ways to make LLM search and shopping assistants act in the consumer's interest: debiasing agent choices (position, brand, anchoring), eliciting and representing user preferences for delegation, fiduciary or principal-agent alignment of AI shopping agents, disclosure and labeling of sponsored content in LLM answers, robustness to seller manipulation, and mechanism or market design for agent-mediated commerce? Which interventions have measured effects?
streams.extra: Read first: workbench/agents/04_brand_bias_manipulation.md, 05_llm_agents_as_shoppers.md and 07_hci_trust_reliance.md. Output file names use prefix f1_4.
